Security Effect v0.14 validation
===============================
Date: 2026-09-01
Status: PROVISIONAL CANDIDATE — STATIC/PACKAGE QUALIFICATION COMPLETE; ooRexx EXECUTABLE QUALIFICATION PENDING

Purpose
-------
v0.14 closes the time-of-check/time-of-irreversible-use gap for staged or long-running operations.
A Security ALLOW at the original method admission is not a bearer capability for a later commit.
The commit must bind the exact continuation, origin execution-evidence identity, operation, staged-state identity,
context, fresh commit invocation evidence, fresh Security snapshot/assessment and (optionally) Access Permissions authority.

New schemas
-----------
Component API:                 security.effect/0.14
Security decision policy:      security.policy/0.5 (unchanged)
Invocation policy:             security.invocation.policy/0.1 (unchanged)
Invocation binding:            security.invocation.binding/0.1 (unchanged)
Continuation policy:           security.continuation.policy/0.1
Continuation binding/evidence: security.continuation.binding/0.1

Static/package gates completed
------------------------------
PASS: four shipped shell runners pass `bash -n`.
PASS: v0.14 static commit-contract audit.
PASS: core runner declares 30 executable Rexx tests, including test_commit_revalidation.rex.
PASS: Access Permissions runner declares four direct tests plus the existing live Alchemy invocation integration test.
PASS: source contains explicit exact-state, exact-context, fresh-snapshot, current-disposition and single-use replay barriers.
PASS: continuation requires non-empty host-supplied origin execution-evidence identity; Security validation alone is not represented as proof that work started.
PASS: combined continuation/invocation consumption is fail-closed and contains no replay-barrier rollback path.
PASS: decision policy schema remains security.policy/0.5; this cut changes continuation/commit execution evidence, not Bouncer rule meaning.
PASS: no runtime LLM decision path introduced.

Executable gates prepared but NOT claimed in this environment
--------------------------------------------------------------
- 30 core Security Effect tests.
- Interaction Event v0.3 integrations.
- Relationship Case v0.2 / Service v0.1 integrations.
- Access Permissions v0.1 integrations including exact COMMIT authority boundary.
- unchanged Access Permissions consumer suite.
- unchanged FederationBank Staff Method Permissions consumer suite when available.
- complete rexxc sweep over shipped .rex/.cls targets.
- commit revalidation demo.

Why executable certification is pending
---------------------------------------
The ooRexx 5.3.0 r13196 executable used for all prior Security Effect certification is not present in this execution
filesystem, and no rexx/rexxc executable is on PATH. Previous v0.13 executable PASS evidence is retained as predecessor
evidence only and is not relabelled as v0.14 execution.

The user-supplied authoritative outer roll-up oorexxapis(20260901-104840).zip was declared at
/mnt/data/oorexxapis(20260901-104840).zip but that exact path did not materialise in either the container or Python
filesystem view. Therefore no byte-preserving September-1 outer-roll-up replacement or dependency-version claim is made.

Current standalone dependency declaration remains the last physically qualified v0.13 line until the new roll-up bytes
can be inspected:
- Institutional Policy v0.8
- Alchemy Objects v0.8
- ooRexx Crypto v0.5
Integration companions:
- Interaction Event v0.3
- Relationship Case v0.2
- Relationship Case Service v0.1
- ooRexx Access Permissions v0.1

Trust-boundary non-claims
-------------------------
- SecurityContinuationEvidence is not Permission authority.
- originExecutionEvidenceIdentity is host/enforcement provenance; Security Effect does not reinterpret it as authority.
- SecurityCommitEvidence is not proof that a transaction was actually published.
- SecurityCommitValidation is not method authority.
- Permission ALLOW remains separately required where Access Permissions governs the COMMIT method.
- physical commit/publication remains the host/enforcement responsibility.
- no certification claim is made for the inaccessible 20260901 outer roll-up.
